capturedPrompts.space:
REFERENCE LOCK
Use the attached Dakk fantasy reference ONLY for confident oil brushwork, believable weight, rich surface painting, warm/cool lighting, deep shadow and selective focal detail. Create an ORIGINAL science-fiction painting. Do not copy any depicted character, creature, weapon, costume, pose arrangement, contact-sheet layout or checkerboard. This is one proposed SPACE STYLE REFERENCE for human approval, not final game assets.

FROZEN STYLE (PROPOSED frontier-oil-01)
Classic painted science-fiction adventure illustration: confident visible oil brushwork, grounded heroic realism and convincing industrial mass. Rich charcoal, worn ivory, oxidised copper and muted mineral colours, shaped by dramatic warm-versus-cool lighting and deep chiaroscuro. Weathered ceramic hulls, scorched metal, scratched observation glass, patched pressure suits and layered mechanical detail. The focal silhouette and identifying structures are crisp; secondary surfaces soften into broad painterly strokes. Alien places feel ancient, immense and mysterious. Serious, adventurous and quietly ominous, never cute or cartoonish, never glossy product-render CGI. High-detail oil illustration with a clear hierarchy of light, shape and texture.

SUBJECT
One coherent painted scene on an ancient rocky alien frontier at dusk. In the foreground stands a memorable silver-grey wolf-like terrestrial canid with amber eyes, a clear anatomically canine muzzle, two upright ears, exactly four rooted legs and a bushy dark-tipped tail. It has proud, alert, intelligent character and believable dense fur, not a toy or mascot. One adult human explorer in a worn ivory-and-charcoal pressure suit stands a respectful short distance behind it, visor open enough for an expressive face. A small weathered survey spacecraft rests in the middle distance: broad ceramic cargo spine, exactly two blunt engine pods, one offset dark observation cockpit, no weapons. Vast eroded charcoal and ochre stone formations and sparse strange rooted vegetation frame the distance; one immense ochre planet hangs above a thin clouded horizon. The juxtaposition gives intimate creature character and an immense mysterious universe.

COUNTS AND DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
Exactly one canid, one adult explorer, one small ship and one distant planet. Natural coherent anatomy. Canid coat silver grey with warm ivory muzzle and a dark tail tip; no horns, armor, jewellery, wings, glowing parts or magic. Suit and ship show layered industrial construction, scuffed ceramic, oxidised copper and repaired surfaces. The new ship is a style-test design, not an existing game chassis. Paint the creature as a distinctive living organism; do not add fantasy weapons or D&D clothing.

LAYOUT
A single landscape oil illustration, not a grid or collage. The complete foreground canid is large enough to inspect, shown in a grounded three-quarter side view, looking toward the viewer. Keep its muzzle, all four paws, ears and tail fully within the frame. Explorer and ship support it at different depth scales. Warm low grazing light from upper left, cool shadow masses on the right; vivid but restrained mineral colors. Clear focal hierarchy and readable silhouettes. Visible directional brush marks; secondary detail softens with distance.

TECHNICAL OUTPUT
One opaque landscape PNG, approximately 1536x1024 if supported. This is an opaque environment/style-reference profile: paint the scene edge to edge. No transparency or magenta key background. No text or UI.

PROFILE-SPECIFIC NEGATIVE
No checkerboard, contact-sheet panels, labels, titles, logos, watermarks, frames, collage, miniature copies of the reference, medieval weapons, fantasy costume, cute cartoon mascot, glossy CGI, plastic figurine, photoreal product render, neon cyberpunk interface, vector look, malformed anatomy, extra limbs, cropped creature parts, excessive bloom or flat airbrushed surfaces.
capturedPrompts.biomes:
REFERENCE LOCK
Use the attached original Celestial Frontier landscape ONLY as a reference for painterly surface treatment, believable material mass, selective detail and warm/cool light. Do not repeat its Wolf, person, ship, mesas, orange planet, composition or desert palette. This is a new provisional art-direction comparison requested by Nick, not approved production art.

STYLE
Original mature painted science-fiction exploration art. Visible confident oil brushwork, atmospheric depth, controlled mineral colours, compelling alien biology, selectively sharp focal shapes, soft painted distant forms. Rich and mysterious, approachable through wonder rather than comedy. Each panel needs a genuinely different palette and ecology while still feeling like the same game. Avoid photographic composites, glossy 3D-render plastic, identical orange sunsets, copied fantasy architecture and generic neon.

SUBJECT AND LAYOUT
One polished landscape contact sheet with FOUR equally sized LANDSCAPE paintings in a precise 2 by 2 grid with thin charcoal gutters. No text anywhere, no labels, no inset diagrams. Fill the panels; no outer white margins. Each scene has a convincing navigable ground or shoreline foreground suitable for a future shallow three-quarter turn-based encounter, an atmospheric midground and a distant horizon. Environment studies, not game screenshots. No UI, no heroes, no ships, no foreground featured animals. Distinct rooted botanical life is allowed only where specified. Suggested overall 1536 by 1024 or larger.

TOP LEFT — TERRAN RAINFOREST STUDY
An immense rain-soaked alien rainforest. Dark jade and moss-green canopy; giant buttressed trunks with coherent branching, pale ivory fronds and copper-orange seed pods. A shallow clear stream curves beside a broad dark stone shelf in the foreground. Fine mist and cool silver daylight pierce the canopy. Sparse bioluminescent spores remain subtle. Dense, old, lush and alive, with readable silhouettes rather than visual noise.

TOP RIGHT — ICE CRYOGEYSER STUDY
A vast ice world under blue-grey daylight. Glacial turquoise fractures, enormous sculpted blue-ice ridges, weathered dark rock islands and exactly two distant white cryogeyser plumes. An indigo mountain horizon and a pale crescent moon. A stable snow-dusted slate shelf crosses the foreground. No forest, no flowers, no fantasy crystal cluster or lava. Hostile but breathtaking; broad quiet shapes contrast the rainforest density.

BOTTOM LEFT — OCEAN CORAL/ARCHIPELAGO STUDY
A temperate alien ocean shoreline at pearlescent early morning. Deep teal water, pale limestone terraces, tide pools and tall rust-red porous reef forms visibly rooted below the shallows. A broad gently sloping rock shelf in front, scattered rounded shell-like mineral deposits, offshore limestone islands emerging from lavender sea haze. Organic branching coral must read as marine habitat, not decorative crystals. Reflected soft rose and silver light; no tropical Earth palm trees.

BOTTOM RIGHT — LAVA BASALT STUDY
An airless-looking volcanic basin with no living plants: weathered black basalt columns, cooled wrinkled flows, a few narrow molten amber fissures, mineral-red slopes and distant volcanic haze. Preserve a large solid dark foreground shelf; no lava lake swallowing the playable ground. Ash-grey sky with an enormous distant cratered moon, rusty reflected glow kept local. Dramatic, dangerous and monumental, with cool deep shadows and selective ember accents rather than uniform orange.

TECHNICAL AND NEGATIVES
Opaque finished painted reference PNG, not transparent, no chroma key, no checkerboard. Four and only four separated scenes. No text, typography, logos, watermarks, arrows, panels inside panels, creatures, people, spacecraft, castles, magic runes, oversized mushrooms in every scene, lens flare or uniform colour filter. Do not imply these are pixel-exact generated game seeds; these are art-direction studies drawn from existing biome families.
capturedPrompts.universe:
REFERENCE LOCK
Use the attached Celestial Frontier landscape only to inherit its rich hand-painted science-fiction visual language, material depth and selective detail. Do not copy the Wolf, explorer, ship, landscape composition or repeat the same ochre world. This is a PROVISIONAL visual reference sheet requested for comparison, not approved production art or a procedural runtime output.

STYLE
Original painted space exploration, visible oil brushwork, believable planetary forms, carefully graded atmospheric edges and shadows. Rich mineral colour with controlled luminous accents against deep blue-charcoal space. Beautiful astronomical variety without neon rainbow overload, flat vector icons, glossy product CGI or photographic collage.

LAYOUT
A clean landscape reference sheet, 4 columns by 2 rows, EIGHT separated object studies of equal visual importance. Thin charcoal gutters and consistent near-black opaque space backgrounds. No text, no captions, no symbols, no frames within frames. Each object fully inside its cell with generous margins. Maintain a consistent light from upper left for externally illuminated bodies; self-luminous stars glow from their own surfaces. Show actual distinct silhouettes, including rings where specified. These are proposal archetypes, not claims of exact seeded instances. Approximate 1536x1024 or larger.

TOP ROW LEFT TO RIGHT
1. TERRAN PLANET: round blue-green ocean world with irregular ochre/olive continents, thin layered white weather systems, subtle azure atmosphere and readable night-side terminator; richly painted but not a copy of Earth.
2. RINGED GAS GIANT: broad cream, muted copper and charcoal atmospheric bands with one distinct oval storm, wide tilted dusty ivory rings, planet correctly occluding rear rings and a physically convincing ring shadow. No solid continents.
3. ICE WORLD: pearl-white and deep cyan sphere, giant ice fractures, a few slate exposed regions, pale blue limb, crisp but restrained lighting; no oceans or green vegetation.
4. LAVA WORLD: dark red-black crust sphere crossed by a few connected molten fissures, cooled basalt plates, narrow ember glow, believable round volume; no decorative rune pattern.

BOTTOM ROW LEFT TO RIGHT
5. GOLDEN MAIN-SEQUENCE STAR: granular gold-ivory self-luminous orb, irregular surface texture and restrained painterly corona; no planetary cast shadow or halo-obscured face.
6. PROTOSTAR: warm central forming star within a broad thin dusty copper accretion disk, outer disk dark and inner regions luminous, angled shallow three-quarter; clearly different from the ringed gas planet, no planet or extra companion.
7. BLACK HOLE: dark central silhouette wrapped by a luminous tilted accretion disk with the far disk visibly bending above and below from lensing; legible restrained gold-white plasma, black center, no portal/runes or purple fantasy vortex.
8. SPIRAL GALAXY: a distant entire spiral galaxy in an angled disc, warm ivory core, two broad soft blue-grey arms, patchy rust dust lanes and subtle scattered star-forming knots; full silhouette kept inside its cell and recognizably immense, not a gas cloud ball.

TECHNICAL OUTPUT
A single opaque full-colour PNG. No transparency or magenta extraction, no checkerboard, no labels, no starfield clutter over the objects, no text or watermarks. Individual surfaces must remain legible at small reference-sheet size. Do not repeat one planet eight times. This sheet reviews silhouettes, palette, light and painted treatment; it is not a physically-scaled orbital scene or a usable layered sprite atlas.

decision: Nick requested additional comparisons before confirming; initial approval question remains unaccepted.
